slides.heading: Bst Traversal
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Search Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Bst Traversal, a medium binary search trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: In-order, pre-order and post-order traversals appending into a list.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. In-order, pre-order and post-order traversals appending into a list.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: In-order, pre-order and post-order differ only in when the node is visited relative to its children.
slides.narration: In-order, pre-order and post-order differ only in when the node is visited relative to its children.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: All three are O(n) time, O(h) stack
Iterative versions use an explicit stack
slides.narration: All three traversals visit every node once, linear time, with recursion depth equal to the height. The only difference is when we record the node relative to its children.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, in-order: left, node, right. Second, pre-order: node, left, right. Third, post-order: left, right, node.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: In-order (left, node, right): [1, 2, 5, 5, 10, 15, 22]
slides.narration: In-order, left, node, right: 1, 2, 5, 5, 10, 15, 22. Notice in-order gives sorted values.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Each method checks for null, then the only difference is the line that adds the value: between the recursive calls for in-order, before them for pre-order, and after them for post-order.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: In-order of a BST = sorted order
Deep trees can overflow the call stack
slides.narration: In-order traversal of a BST yields sorted values. Very deep trees can overflow the call stack, so know the iterative versions.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Pre-order serialises/copies a tree; post-order deletes/evaluates
Follow-up: Morris traversal with O(1) space
slides.narration: Pre-order is used to copy or serialise a tree; post-order to delete it or evaluate expressions. Morris traversal achieves constant space.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: In-order, pre-order and post-order differ only in when the node is visited relative to its children.
slides.narration: To recap Bst Traversal: In-order, pre-order and post-order differ only in when the node is visited relative to its children. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
